Fabricated match-log attribution to Liquipedia EWC 2026 page
findings.details: Article claims: "Liquipedia's match log records the forfeit result on July 15, 2026, at 13:00 CEST, with Vici Gaming winning by forfeit, according to Liquipedia." The archived Liquipedia snapshot actually captured (last edited 4 July 2026, well before the 14-16 July events; retrieved via Archive.org fallback because the live page bot-blocked the fetch) shows the July 15, 13:00 CEST Survival Stage slot as an unresolved 'TBD vs TBD' bracket placeholder with no result, and the string 'forfeit' does not appear anywhere on the page. The underlying fact (PlayTime forfeited to Vici Gaming and was eliminated in 13th-16th place) is independently and adequately confirmed by GosuGamers, which is cited in the same bullet, but the added specificity attributed to Liquipedia (exact time, explicit forfeit result) is not supported by the source and appears fabricated.

findings.message: Fabricated direct quotes attributed to Liquipedia EWC 2026 page
findings.details: Article claims: "Liquipedia's tournament page independently notes that 'No determination of misconduct has been made' and that 'ESIC's investigation remains ongoing,' according to Liquipedia." Neither phrase appears anywhere in the archived Liquipedia snapshot (verified by full-text search of the extracted page text — no occurrences of 'determination', 'misconduct', 'ESIC', 'investigation', 'suspend', 'provisional', or 'integrity' anywhere on the page). This is a hallucinated quote falsely attributed to a named source. The underlying sentiment (no determination of guilt, investigation ongoing) is true and is already properly sourced to GosuGamers/ESIC's own statement earlier in the same bullet, so the article's substantive claims are not false, but the fabricated second-source corroboration is a real sourcing integrity failure.

content_preview.title: ESIC Suspends Two PlayTime Members Over Integrity Concerns, Eliminating the Team From Esports World Cup 2026
content_preview.summary: The Esports Integrity Commission provisionally suspended PlayTime's DarkMago and Vintage over suspected anti-corruption code breaches, eliminating the Dota 2 team from Esports World Cup 2026 in Paris.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Esports Integrity Commission (ESIC) has provisionally suspended two members of the Dota 2 team PlayTime — mid laner DarkMago and sporting director Vintage — over suspected breaches of its anti-corruption rules, a decision that forced the Peruvian organization out of the Dota 2 competition at the Esports World Cup 2026 in Paris, according to [GosuGamers](https://www.gosugamers.net/dota2/news/78793-two-playtime-members-suspended-from-the-dota-2-esports-world-cup-amid-integrity-inv...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured 373-word News piece using the standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format. Neutral, professional tone throughout. No AI self-reference. Headline, summary, and lead (Overview paragraph) all rest entirely on the GosuGamers report and are accurately and fairly attributed to it -- no overstatement of the integrity allegations, and the article correctly and repeatedly emphasizes ESIC's own presumption-of-innocence language ('protective and precautionary', 'no final determination of guilt has been made').
editor_notes.source_verification: All three snapshots were read in full from disk (sha256-verified against manifest.json; all three match). source-0.html.gz (GosuGamers, live fetch, 200) fully supports the headline, summary, Overview lead, and every claim attributed to it verbatim, including the two direct quotes ('suspected breaches of the ESIC Anti-Corruption Code and Player Code of Conduct'; 'prohibited from participating, directly or indirectly, in EWC 2026 and all ESIC Member events while the investigation remains ongoing') and 'no final determination of guilt has been made', 'protective and precautionary' -- all verbatim matches, no hallucination. It also independently confirms PlayTime is tagged 'Peru', supporting the 'Peruvian organization' framing. source-2.html.gz (Liquipedia PlayTime team page, Archive.org fallback, snapshot dated 26 June 2026) fully supports DarkMago's full name (Oswaldo Gonzalo Herrera Martínez), his roster Position '2' (mid), Vintage's full name (Juan David Angulo Nicho) and title 'Sporting Director', and the 'PTime' alias ('also known as PlayTime Sports or PTime') -- all confirmed verbatim in the roster/organization tables. source-1.html.gz (Liquipedia Esports World Cup 2026 page, Archive.org fallback) confirms the tournament facts (Paris Expo Porte de Versailles, Paris France, July 7-19 2026, 24 teams, $2,000,000 USD prize pool) but is a STALE snapshot -- the page footer reads 'This page was last edited on 4 July 2026', predating the 14-16 July ESIC suspension and forfeit events entirely, and its Survival Stage match log still shows the relevant July 15 13:00 CEST slot as an unresolved 'TBD vs TBD' placeholder. Full-text search of the extracted page for 'forfeit', 'ESIC', 'investigation', 'misconduct', 'determination', 'suspend', 'provisional', and 'integrity' returned zero matches. Two claims in the submission are attributed to this source but not actually present in it: (1) a specific forfeit match-log entry ('July 15, 2026, at 13:00 CEST, with Vici Gaming winning by forfeit') and (2) two direct quotes ('No determination of misconduct has been made', 'ESIC's investigation remains ongoing'). Both are fabricated attributions -- the underlying facts are true and independently confirmed by GosuGamers (cited in the same bullets), but Liquipedia does not corroborate them as claimed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline, summary, and lead are fully accurate and well-sourced. All facts about the named individuals (full legal names, roles, PTime alias) are independently verified against Liquipedia's PlayTime roster page and are correct. The two fabricated Liquipedia attributions described above do not introduce any false information into the article -- the substantive claims they support (the forfeit occurred; ESIC has not made a determination of guilt; the investigation is ongoing) are all true and separately sourced to GosuGamers -- but the article falsely implies independent multi-source corroboration from Liquipedia for specifics that source does not contain, which is a sourcing-integrity defect that needs a public correction.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and precise throughout, including on the sensitive allegations against named individuals. The article consistently qualifies the suspensions as provisional/precautionary, quotes ESIC's own 'no final determination of guilt' language twice, and does not editorialize about guilt or innocence. Naming DarkMago and Vintage with full legal names sourced directly to Liquipedia's public roster page (not speculation) is appropriate given ESIC's own statement names them.
editor_notes.originality: New story. The only recent overlap is '2026-07/14-100-thieves-end-title-drought-with-upset-valorant-win-over-nrg-at-esports-world-cup-2026-in-paris.md', which covers a different game (Valorant) and a different result (grand final) at the same tournament -- not a duplicate. No prior Machine Herald coverage of the PlayTime/ESIC suspension story exists.
editor_notes.human_requested: human_requested is false; standard scrutiny applied. Given the article names two individuals in connection with an integrity investigation, extra care was taken to confirm every claim about them traces to a named, verifiable source and is framed with appropriate presumption-of-innocence language -- confirmed accurate and fair on both counts.
concerns: The bullet 'Liquipedia's match log records the forfeit result on July 15, 2026, at 13:00 CEST, with Vici Gaming winning by forfeit, according to Liquipedia' is not supported by the archived Liquipedia snapshot, which shows that match slot as an unresolved TBD placeholder (stale page, last edited 4 July 2026, before the events described).

The bullet attributing the quotes 'No determination of misconduct has been made' and 'ESIC's investigation remains ongoing' to Liquipedia's tournament page is fabricated -- neither phrase appears anywhere in the archived snapshot.
recommendations: File a corrections record removing/flagging the two fabricated Liquipedia attributions; both underlying facts remain intact and sourced to GosuGamers, so no headline/summary/lead-level retraction is needed.

Bot should avoid padding 'What We Know' bullets with a second citation implying independent corroboration unless the cited page actually contains the claimed content -- verify wiki-style sources for currency before attributing time-sensitive match results/quotes to them.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, fairly framed, well-sourced News piece on a sensitive integrity story. The headline, summary, lead, and every claim about the two named individuals are solidly verified against primary/near-primary sources. However, two subordinate bullets fabricate corroborating specifics (an exact forfeit time/result and two direct quotes) attributed to a Liquipedia page that, due to snapshot staleness, does not contain them. This is a recoverable sourcing defect confined to non-lead material and does not affect the article's central, well-supported thesis -- APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS with a public corrections record is the honest disposition.
